title: Tensoring with a pro-etale locally finite free internal module preserves finite limits
statement: Let X be a scheme, R a commutative internal ring in abelian sheaves on its pro-etale site, and P an internal R-module [def-weil-pbc-condensed-e-module-category, def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. Suppose a pro-etale covering C of X makes each pullback of P finite free. Then the ordinary module tensor functor Mod.tensorLeft P preserves every finite limit. No noetherianity or coefficient-field hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Declaration docstring: evaluation on K-injective resolutions and locally finite free tensor calculation; Stacks 08JJ and HRS Lemma 5.3(2)

proof.text: For P isomorphic to R^n, the tensor-Hom adjunction identifies its right adjoint with the finite-power functor. The finite-copower functor is another left adjoint of that finite-power functor, so uniqueness of left adjoints identifies tensor with finite copower. In an abelian category finite copower is also finite power and therefore preserves finite limits. The argument also works for n=0.

proof.text: Pullback of internal modules along any scheme morphism commutes with tensor: transport the parallel-pair coequalizer defining relative tensor using the strong braided monoidal pullback and preservation of coequalizers. Pullback preserves finite limits, since its underlying sheaf functor does and the module forgetful functor creates and reflects limits.

source.place: Declaration docstring: evaluation on K-injective resolutions and locally finite free tensor calculation; Stacks 08JJ and HRS Lemma 5.3(2)

proof.text: For a finite diagram, pull its limit-comparison map back along every member of the trivializing cover. By the tensor-pullback isomorphism and the finite-free calculation the pulled-back comparison is invertible. These pullbacks jointly reflect isomorphisms: on underlying sheaves, use the covering sieve obtained by base change to each pro-etale object and the sheaf local-isomorphism criterion; the module forgetful functor reflects isomorphisms. Hence the original limit comparison is invertible, proving preservation of the limit.

lean.statement:
theorem condensed_locally_free_tensor_preservesFiniteLimits {X : Scheme.{u}}
    (R : Sheaf (Scheme.ProEt.topology X) Ab.{u + 1}) [MonObj R] [IsCommMonObj R]
    (P : Mod (Sheaf (Scheme.ProEt.topology X) Ab.{u + 1}) R)
    (hP : ∃ C : Scheme.Cover.{u} Scheme.proetalePrecoverage X, ∀ s : C.I₀,
      Mod.IsFree ((upperStar Ab.{u + 1} (C.f s)).obj R)
        (((upperStar Ab.{u + 1} (C.f s)).mapMod R).obj P)) :
    PreservesFiniteLimits (Mod.tensorLeft P)
